newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares close down in sluggish trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares close down in sluggish trading.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended down in sluggish trading on Thursday with most investors remaining on the sidelines due to a lack of fresh stimuli, brokers said.
The index edged down 0.044 points or 0.09 percent to 48.648 points on volume of 3.1 million shares worth $886,000. Of 41 B shares, 31 traded with 11 down, 11 flat and nine up.
Brokers said both selling and buying were light in the sluggish market, and the market would continue to be bearish.
"Third-tier stocks suffered big losses with investors losing confidence in their ability to improve their results in the short-term," one broker said.
"The market will fall further until it finds support at 48 points," a second broker said.
Shanghai Rubber Belt was the worst performer on institutional liquidation, plunging $0.038 or 25.00 percent to $0.114 on volume of 112,000 shares.

Huaxin Cement followed on the expectation of unpromising results, falling $0.010 or 4.54 percent to $0.210 on volume of 30,000 shares in the morning session and did not trade in the second half of the session.
Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor traded the most on overseas selling and domestic institutional support. It fell $0.002 or 0.43 percent to $0.462 on volume of 422,000 shares.

Shanghai A shares soared following corrections over the past few days with fresh capital inflow spurred by a positive speech a senior securities official in Beijing, brokers said, adding that it would maintain its bullish tone.

Zhou Zhengqing, chairman of the policy-making Securities Commission under the State Council, said the stock markets provided support for the economy in a wide variety of ways including giving firms a means of raising funds.

The A index jumped 32.359 points or 3.53 percent to 949.768 points on volume of 937.4 million shares worth 6.9 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index rose 67.729 points or 2.79 percent to 2494.798 points.
Chengdu Gongyi Metallurgy was the star on speculative buying, surging 1.01 yuan or 24.63 percent to 5.11 yuan on volume of 30.7 million shares.
